field_evidence_note: Each index names the dossier evidence item that actually supports the canonical field; the promotion step emits one formal evidence row per field/index pair.
limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No memcached server, client library or Django test suite was run; the finding is static. The regression test was read, not executed.
Reachability requires an application to pass externally influenced strings as cache keys. Applications that only cache trusted, generated keys are not exposed.

The advisories describe the impact generically as a key collision; the precise wire-level collision behaviour depends on the memcached client library and the ASCII protocol's space-delimited key parsing. No client library was exercised to confirm a specific collision payload.

NVD and GHSA both assign CWE-295 (Improper Certificate Validation), which does not describe a cache-key validation flaw. No source in the collected families assigns a cache-key-specific CWE. The canonical value follows the sources rather than replacing them, and this mismatch is recorded as a source defect.
GHSA database_specific calls the severity HIGH while its own CVSS 3.1 vector scores 5.9 and NVD rates it 5.9 MEDIUM. The canonical score follows the NVD primary CVSS 3.1 metric.
The MITRE CVE v5 CNA record is a placeholder (vendor/product/version n/a, problemType n/a, no CVSS).

The four fix commits are chained on top of the corresponding CVE-2020-13596 fixes: 2c824149's parent is 2dd4d110, 580bd64c's parent is 49d7cc19, 84b2da55's parent is 1f2dd37f and 07e59caa's parent is 6d61860b. Author dates are 2020-05-20 while committer dates are 2020-06-03, the release-preparation day.
The fix is not uniform: delete_many still calls the client without validate_key, and BaseCache.validate_key remains warn-only. The raising behaviour exists only in BaseMemcachedCache.validate_key.

memcache_key_warnings yields a bare string for the length branch but a (message, CacheKeyWarning) tuple for the character branch, so InvalidCacheKey receives a tuple in the character case. The exception is still raised, but its argument is not a plain string.
The canonical vulnerable commit is the 3.0.2 tag; the 2.2 branch has the same vulnerable code at 2.2.12 but the dataset snapshot for this repository is 3.0.2.
The snapshot inventory has 6163 tracked files and 67 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.
No downstream distribution backport (Ubuntu USN-4381-1/2, Debian DSA-4705, Fedora, NetApp, Oracle) was verified; only upstream tags and commits are used.

critical_operation.description: BaseMemcachedCache.get and BaseMemcachedCache.set take an application-supplied key, convert it with make_key and hand it to the client library without any validation. BaseCache.make_key only applies the key function (prefix and version); BaseCache.validate_key exists but merely emits CacheKeyWarning, and the memcached backend never calls it. The memcached ASCII protocol treats whitespace and control characters as key delimiters, so distinct Django keys that differ only after such a character can reach the server as the same key. A write (set) then overwrites another logical entry, and a later read (get) of either key returns the other entry's value. The 3.0.7/2.2.13 fix adds self.validate_key(key) before every client call and gives BaseMemcachedCache a validate_key that raises InvalidCacheKey.

entry_point.description: An application caches a value under a key it derived from request data. BaseMemcachedCache.set receives the key, and the key reaches the memcached client without validation.

trace.description: make_key returns the key function output without validating characters or length
BaseCache.validate_key only warns on control characters and is not called by the memcached methods
set converts the application key and passes it to the client without a validate_key call
the unvalidated key crosses into the memcached client at line 75; the ASCII protocol then parses it as a space-delimited key
